subject: SLA remedy trigger definition & monthly credit ceiling — clarification
messages:
From: Jordan Mullins <jmullins@cloudpath.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <prao@cloudpath.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify remedy triggers & monthly credit calculation

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the draft SLA (attached). Procurement has a couple of open items we need clarified before we can greenlight:

1) What exactly constitutes a remedy "trigger"? The draft references "service unavailability" but doesn't define the sustained window or cross-region aggregation rules. Can you confirm whether a 15-minute sustained outage in a single region triggers a credit, or whether you require a global aggregation?

2) Monthly credit ceiling: the table lists a percentage-based credit but no cap. Our finance team needs a predictable maximum. Can you provide an example calculation (monthly bill = $475,000) and a hard cap option?

3) Latency SLOs — procurement noticed only availability bands. We need at least a P95 latency target for the inference API (sample workload: 256-token requests, bursty daytime traffic).

We attached a short list of the procurement team's asks (CloudPath_Remedy_Requests.docx). Timeline: we need answers by EOD Friday to hit our December procurement window.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Mullins
Head of Procurement — CloudPath
jmullins@cloudpath.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priya Rao <prao@cloudpath.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify remedy triggers & monthly credit calculation

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front, then details below:
- Remedy trigger: we currently define a trigger as sustained service unavailability > 30 minutes for a single region for regionally isolated outages, or any multi-region sustained impact > 15 minutes for cross-region failure modes. We can tighten/loosen per request.
- Monthly credit ceiling: we typically offer a tiered credit ladder (example attached) with a cap — proposes either 25% of monthly invoice or a flat dollar cap (you pick). Example calc included.
- Latency SLO: we can include a P95 500ms target for standard inference endpoints; higher-tier critical endpoints can be 250–300ms.

Notes and attachments: I attached Proposed_SLA_Calc_Table.csv showing sample math for a $475k month and two cap options (percentage and flat USD). Laura — looping you for legal/ops language on maintenance carveouts and cap ceilings. Ben — tagging for commercial approval on the proposed cap options.

If that aligns, I'll turn this into a redline we can send back to Jordan for signature.

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Revenue — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachments: Proposed_SLA_Calc_Table.csv, SLA_Draft_CloudPath_2026.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify remedy triggers & monthly credit calculation

Rishi / Ben —

Forwarding Jordan's note and Rishi's proposals. A few legal ops points we should standardize before sending a redline:

- Maintenance carveouts: define routine maintenance windows (we usually allow a 4-hour weekly window per region; any announced maintenance within that window is carved out). Emergency maintenance must be notified within 2 hours and will not be considered a credit trigger if mitigation begins within 30 minutes of detection and a post-mortem is provided within 72 hours.

- Credit cap: from a legal risk perspective, recommend offering the lower of (a) 25% of monthly invoice OR (b) $100k flat cap for the initial 12-month term. This limits exposure while giving CloudPath predictability.

- Remedy trigger window: Rishi's 30-minute regional / 15-minute multi-region baseline seems reasonable, but procurement may push for shorter windows. Suggest we mark the trigger as: "sustained unavailability for a contiguous period of at least 30 minutes in a single region, or any contiguous period of at least 15 minutes affecting more than one region."

- Latency commitments: recommend P95 500ms standard with an opt-in 99th percentile for premium endpoints only.

If you want me to edit the draft SLA language, I can push a redline tonight.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Mullins <jmullins@cloudpath.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <prao@cloudpath.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 12:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify remedy triggers & monthly credit calculation

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups so we can brief finance/legal: 

1) Endpoint split: CloudPath's platform has two classes of traffic. Can we split the SLA so that control-plane APIs (authentication, model management) get a 99.95% uptime target while inference/serving endpoints remain at 99.90%? We'd be comfortable with different credit ladders per class.

2) Remedy trigger window: procurement is asking whether you can commit to 30 minutes for regional and 10 minutes for multi-region. If not, we'll accept 15 minutes for multi-region as a compromise. The key is clarity on the measurement window (sliding window vs contiguous).

3) Cap: $100k flat cap would work for the initial term, but finance asked whether we can add an escalation clause tied to volume — e.g., if monthly spend exceeds $750k, increase cap to $250k. Can you confirm you can include that conditional cap?

We're attaching a short doc with what procurement will mark as "non-negotiable" (CloudPath_Remedy_Requests.docx). Would appreciate a redline back today if possible — procurement is running the approval window tight.

Jordan

Attachments: CloudPath_Remedy_Requests.docx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotma@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mullins <jmullins@cloudpath.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 15:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify remedy triggers & monthly credit calculation — Redwood proposal

Jordan —

Thanks for the specifics — we can work with that. Proposed redlines below (high level):

1) Endpoint split: agree to split SLA by endpoint class. Control-plane endpoints: 99.95% monthly uptime. Inference endpoints: 99.90% monthly uptime. Separate credit ladders will apply.

2) Remedy trigger window: we will accept a 30-minute contiguous window for single-region impact. For multi-region impact we will accept a 15-minute contiguous window. We cannot commit to a 10-minute multi-region trigger because of measurement noise across edge caches; 15 minutes is our ops-tested threshold. Measurement is based on sliding-window observed availability using production telemetry (details in the appendix).

3) Credit cap: will offer the lower of (a) 25% of monthly invoice OR (b) a flat cap that scales with spend: $100k for monthly spend < $750k; $250k for monthly spend >= $750k. That should match your finance ask.

I've attached a redline PDF (CP_DocuSign_SLA_2026.pdf) and a cleaned-up calculation spreadsheet. If that looks good, I'll send the DocuSign link for signature and route to finance/legal for countersign.

Next steps: Jordan — can you confirm on the endpoint split and the conditional cap? If confirmed, I'll issue the DocuSign and we can aim to close before the end of the week.

Regards,
Rishi
Director, Revenue — Redwood Inference

Attachments: CP_DocuSign_SLA_2026.pdf, Proposed_SLA_Calc_Table.csv
